title: Bootstrap TripForge app skeleton via SDD
body:
Feature-sized — route through Spec Kit (/speckit-specify -> /speckit-plan -> /speckit-tasks -> /speckit-implement).

Stand up the v1 skeleton so every later iteration has a real product to exercise:
- TypeScript monorepo: web app (agent workspace) + API service
- `npm test` (L1 unit) and `npm run lint` wired and passing
- Health endpoint + an L3 smoke script (start real server, hit real routes, assert responses); then set `verification.oracle.smoke_command` in kitchenloop.yaml
- Persistence layer chosen in the plan (Constitution Check applies)

Acceptance: fresh clone -> install -> test/lint/smoke all pass; loop-state and coverage matrix can record a T1 scenario against the running app. Quality tooling wired as devDeps with configs: knip (dead code), jscpd (duplication), dependency-cruiser (.dependency-cruiser.cjs encoding the layer boundaries from .claude/skills/typescript-clean-architecture/SKILL.md).

title: Canonical itinerary schema v0 (Constitution IV) via SDD
body:
Feature-sized — route through Spec Kit.

Define the single versioned itinerary schema that flows through build -> book -> trade:
- Core entities: itinerary, day, item (stay/activity/transfer), media ref, pricing block
- Provenance fields: original author, license terms, revenue-share obligations, rebrand lineage
- JSON Schema (or zod) + TypeScript types + schema version field and migration convention

Acceptance: schema package published inside the repo; builder/booking/marketplace code may only import the itinerary type from this package. No layer may fork or privately extend it.

title: Supply adapter port family + sandbox mocks (Constitution V, PRD 9.3)
body:
Feature-sized — route through Spec Kit.

Create the supplier-agnostic port family for the P0 bookable component map: hotels (bedbank net rates), activities/tickets, transfers, car rental — each with search, quote-with-markup, book, cancel — plus deterministic sandbox mock implementations for tests. Design the port contracts for the PRD 9.2/9.4 engineering realities: quote-then-book with price hold/expiry + re-quote, multi-currency, partial-failure handling in multi-supplier carts, and a merchant-of-record field per component. No supplier API shapes may leak outside an adapter. Real aggregator integrations (RateHawk/Viator/Mozio/CarTrawler class) come later behind the same ports.

Acceptance: booking flows compile against the port interfaces only; L2 contract tests run against the sandbox mocks; swapping implementations requires zero changes outside the adapter package.

title: Budget allocator + quote-then-book flow (PRD 9.1/9.2/9.4) via SDD
body:
Feature-sized — route through Spec Kit. The core AI differentiator per Constitution III.

Budget allocator: split a total budget (hard cap or target) across categories (flights/transport 35-45%, accommodation 30-40%, activities 10-15%, local transport/transfers 5-10%, buffer 5-10% — tunable by trip type), pull live options per category via the supply ports, assemble to fit, re-balance when a category runs over. Output: itinerary (canonical schema) with visible per-category and per-day budget breakdown.

Quote-then-book: price holds with expiry, re-quote on expiry, transparent currency conversion, multi-supplier cart with partial-failure handling (one component fails, others hold).

Acceptance: allocator is a pure domain function (exhaustively tested, integer minor units); plan->book conversion events emitted (PMF metric); L3 test walks describe-trip -> allocated plan -> quote -> book against sandbox mocks with state-delta assertions.

title: Regression oracle: L3 state-delta harness + PMF instrumentation events
body:
Build the 4-layer verification harness (compile -> execute -> parse -> state deltas) for TripForge:
- L3 helpers: start real app + DB, perform an action via API, assert exact DB state deltas (e.g., booking writes reservation + markup ledger rows; failed booking leaves state unchanged — conservation assertion)
- Money-path conservation checks per Constitution VI
- Emit the PMF metrics events from day one: marketplace take-rate revenue per active agent, resold-vs-self-built trip ratio

Acceptance: `verification.oracle.smoke_command` runs the harness in bounded time; quality-bar L3 requirement is enforceable in Polish.
